# My Thinking

I have been farming this land in Quzhou for over forty years. My husband is gone, my son works in Shijiazhuang. I manage the land myself, about 6 mu total, and hire a neighbor with a tractor for heavy work during planting and harvest.

Here there is no question what I will grow. Everyone grows winter wheat followed by summer corn. That is the rotation. The soil and the water are suited for it. I would not try cotton or vegetables on a large scale — at my age, the labor is too much, and I do not know the markets well enough.

For wheat, I will buy the improved seed from the village cooperative store — the same variety I used last year, Jimai 22 or similar. It is reliable. I apply base fertilizer at planting time — compound fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium mixed in — then I top-dress with urea before the rains in April when the wheat starts jointing. I irrigate three times: once before winter dormancy sets in to help the roots establish, once in March when growth resumes, and once at heading. I spray twice — once for powdery mildew in spring, once for aphids near grain fill. The rotary tiller comes through before planting to turn the stalks under.

For corn, I direct-seed right after wheat harvest in June using hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the store has. No-tillage saves me hiring the tractor again. I apply fertilizer at planting and once more when the corn is knee-high. Summer rain usually handles irrigation but I will water twice if it gets dry, as it does some years here. One pesticide application for fall armyworm, which has been a problem these past few years.

I expect maybe 450 jin per mu for wheat and 550 jin per mu for corn if the weather cooperates.
